# #3936: Patch: the AI's mulligan counts a Tribute card's units, so it stops keeping opening hands it cannot play
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the practice AI picks which opening cards to keep, it looks only at their mana cost. A card that also needs two or three of its own units sacrificed looks cheap, so the AI keeps it and throws back cards it could actually play. Holding Blue-Eyes White Felinor (1 mana, sacrifice 2 units), Lava Golem (3 mana, sacrifice 3) and Trigor (3 mana, sacrifice 3), the AI keeps all three, and none of them can be played until it has built a board. Its check that a hand has an early play is also satisfied by the 1-mana Felinor, which is no early play at all. Once this is built, the AI treats such a card as dearer the more units it needs, so the hands it keeps are hands it can start playing. Players notice a stronger opening from the AI in every game where it is dealt a Tribute card, which Stinkyscape+ has many of.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/mulligan.rs:22,55,96,107,121`: every keep rule reads `query_cost(def)`, the mana cost alone (`crates/engine/src/catalog.rs:544`). That includes the bound, the one-drop cap and the early-play check.
- §6.3 Tribute X (`spec/06-keywords.md`): playing the card also sacrifices X of your units. The engine already offers the number, following Nerfs, Buffs and Floats: `jackioh_engine::play_choices::tribute_cost_of` (`crates/engine/src/play_choices.rs:821`).
- The catalog holds 37 non-token Tribute cards, and 16 of them cost 3 or less and so pass the bound (`AI_MULLIGAN.keep_max_cost` 3, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:999`). They include Blue-Eyes White Felinor (1, Tribute 2), Windfast (1, T1), Raven (0, T1), Lava Golem and Trigor (3, T3), and Stinkyscape+'s Tribute line: Fortress, Zenith, Scepter, Antumbra, Quad, Sei and Vela.
- The shadow ban is empty (`crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs:58`), so every one of them reaches the AI's decks, and Stinkyscape+'s fullsend deals the AI the whole set.

## Proposal

- In the AI's own keep (`mulligan_keep_curved` and the `mulligan_keep_shaped` it calls), read a card's mulligan cost as the larger of its mana cost and its Tribute plus a named per-unit allowance in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (for example Tribute + 1).
- Then a Tribute 3 three-drop falls past the bound, and a 1-mana Tribute 2 card counts neither as a one-drop nor as the early play.
- Leave `mulligan_keep` itself alone: the frozen greedy baseline calls it (`crates/ai/src/baselines.rs:35`) and must not move.
- It reads only the AI's own hand (CLAUDE.md, crates/ai: hidden cards never change a decision).
- Write the reading as a ruling in the issue's block beside R2977000's bound, and update the mulligan paragraph of `crates/ai/README.md`.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/mulligan.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/README.md`
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/decide.rs` (`mod the_mulligans_curve`, its `mulligan_with` helper at `:399`)
- SPEC §9.9 (the practice AI), through `spec/pending/<issue>.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test dealing meditative-025, core-055 and traininggrounds-025 beside cheap plain cards has the AI send back Lava Golem and Trigor and not count Felinor as its early play. It fails today.
- [ ] A Tribute card whose Tribute a Nerf or Floats brought to 0 is kept by its mana cost alone.
- [ ] The greedy baseline's mulligan is unchanged and its tests pass.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` and `cargo jackioh gate` pass, and `cargo jackioh spec check` is green with the new ruling and its test.

## Size and risks

Small: one module, a constant, tests, a README line and a ruling. Difficulty hard (the AI). Low risk: only hands holding a Tribute card are kept differently, which may move pinned AI fixtures or gate games that deal one.
